title: Minimum Health to Beat Game
statement:
A game has `n` levels that must be cleared in order, from level 0 to level `n - 1`. Clearing level `i` costs you `damage[i]` health points.

You also own a piece of armor that you may use on at most one level of your choice; on that level it absorbs up to `armor` points of the damage, so you lose `max(damage[i] - armor, 0)` there instead.

Your health has to stay strictly above 0 at every moment, including after the last level. Return the smallest starting health that lets you clear all the levels.
notes:
## Intuition

Damage only ever takes health away, so your health is lowest after the final level. Without armor you would need `sum(damage) + 1` health to finish with at least 1 left. The armor cuts one level's damage by `min(damage[i], armor)`, and the order of the levels does not matter for the final total, so the best place to use it is the level where it saves the most: the one with the largest damage. A brute force could try the armor on every level and simulate, which is O(n²).

## Approach

1. Walk through `damage` once, adding each `hit` to `total` and tracking the `biggest` hit.
2. The armor saves `saved = min(biggest, armor)`: it cannot block more than the hit itself, nor more than its own strength.
3. Return `total - saved + 1`, the damage you actually take plus the 1 point you must keep.

## Example 1, step by step

`damage = [2, 7, 4, 3]`, `armor = 4`. The loop gives `total = 16` and `biggest = 7`. The armor can absorb at most 4 of the 7, so `saved = min(7, 4) = 4`. You take 12 damage in all and need 1 more to stay alive: the answer is `16 - 4 + 1 = 13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over the levels.
- Space: O(1): just three numbers.

## Pitfalls

- Health must stay strictly positive, so add 1; returning `total - saved` is off by one.
- When `armor` exceeds the biggest hit, only that hit is cancelled; the leftover armor protects nothing else.
- The sum can reach 10^10, so Java and C need a 64-bit `long` for `total`.
- Using the armor on the first or last level makes no difference by itself; only the size of the hit matters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | sum of all damage without armor |
| `biggest` | the largest single hit |
| `hit` | damage of the level being read |
| `saved` | damage the armor absorbs on the biggest hit |

narration.2: Start the running sum of damage at zero.
narration.3: The largest hit so far; damage is never negative, so 0 is a safe start.
narration.4: Visit every level once; the order does not matter for the final health.
narration.5: Add this level's damage to the total.
narration.6: Remember the largest hit, where the armor saves the most.
narration.8: The armor absorbs the whole biggest hit or its full strength, whichever is smaller.
narration.9: Take the remaining damage and add 1 so health ends strictly above zero.
